facts.statement: Tuarangisaurus is an extinct genus of elasmosaurid plesiosaur found in New Zealand and Argentina.
facts.quote: Tuarangisaurus ( "ancient" + "lizard") is an extinct genus of elasmosaurid known from New Zealand and Argentina.

facts.statement: The only known species, Tuarangisaurus keyesi, was named by Wiffen and Moisley in 1986.
facts.quote: The type and only known species is Tuarangisaurus keyesi, named by "Pont" Wiffen, Joan Wiffen and Bill Moisley in 1986.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was collected by amateur paleontologists on March 20, 1978, from the Maungataniwha Sandstone Member of the Tahora Formation.
facts.quote: It was on 20 March 1978 collected by amateur paleontologists from the Maungataniwha Sandstone Member of the Tahora Formation, dating to the upper Campanian to lower Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: A juvenile specimen attributed to Tuarangisaurus contained at least thirty gastroliths.
facts.quote: Some postcranial remains of juveniles were also provisionally attributed to Tuarangisaurus, with one specimen (NZGS CD427) containing at least thirty gastroliths.

facts.statement: In 2026, O'Gorman, Scasso, and Medina assigned an elasmosaurid specimen from the Lefipán Formation of Argentina to Tuarangisaurus keyesi.
facts.quote: In 2026, O'Gorman, Scasso and Medina assigned an elasmosaurid specimen MPEF-PV 12001 from the Lefipán Formation of Argentina to T. keyesi.

facts.statement: A complete specimen of Tuarangisaurus measures over 8 meters in length.
facts.quote: Tuarangisaurus was a medium-sized plesiosaur, with a complete specimen (CM Zfr 115) measuring over 8 m long.

facts.statement: The preserved skull of Tuarangisaurus measured about 37.0 cm long, with an estimated total skull length of 37.5 cm.
facts.quote: The preserved skull measured about 37.0 cm long, and its total skull length is estimated to have been 37.5 cm long.

facts.statement: Tuarangisaurus is distinguished by a unique combination of traits, including an ectopterygoid with a long process directed backward and a large boss of bone underneath.
facts.quote: It can be distinguished from all other known elasmosaurids by a unique combination of characteristics as well as two otherwise unknown traits: the ectopterygoid has a long process directed towards the back, and a large boss of bone underneath.

facts.statement: A stapes bone is present in the holotype, a feature previously thought to be absent in elasmosaurids.
facts.quote: A stapes is present in the holotype; this bone was previously thought to be absent from elasmosaurids.

facts.statement: Tuarangisaurus lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Tuarangisaurus is classified within the family Elasmosauridae.
Tuarangisaurus was originally named by Wiffen and Moisley in 1985.
facts.quote: Fue nombrado originalmente por Wiffen y Moisley en 1985.

facts.statement: The estimated length of Tuarangisaurus is 8 meters.
facts.quote: Se estima su longitud en 8 metros.

facts.statement: The fossil was recovered from the Tahora Formation, dating to the mid-Campanian of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 78 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fue recuperado de los estratos de la formación Tahora, que data de mediados del Campaniense en el Cretácico Superior, hace cerca de 78 millones de años.

facts.statement: In 2026, O'Gorman, Scasso, and Medina reported the first discovery of Tuarangisaurus keyesi fossil material from Maastrichtian strata in the Lefipán Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: O'Gorman, Scasso & Medina (2026) report the first discovery of fossil material of Tuarangisaurus keyesi from the Maastrichtian strata of the Lefipán Formation (Argentina).

rejected.statement: Otero and colleagues redescribed the juvenile specimen NZGS CD427 in 2018 to elucidate the ontogeny of the plesiosaur.
rejected.quote: In 2018, Otero and colleagues redescribed the juvenile specimen NZGS CD427 elucidating the ontogeny of this plesiosaur.

rejected.statement: A 2016 phylogenetic analysis reaffirmed Tuarangisaurus as an elasmosaurid but rejected a close relationship with Callawayasaurus.
rejected.quote: A phylogenetic analysis of plesiosaurs run by O'Gorman and colleagues in 2016 reaffirmed that Tuarangisaurus was an elasmosaurid, but rejected a close relationship with Callawayasaurus.
